Sir Everard J.H. Fraser, K.C.M.G.,
H.B.M.'s Consul-General,
Shanghai.

My dear Sir Everard, Confidential.

In reply to your letter of May 17
regarding the information brought by one Lazar
or Lazear, the following is the result of police
enquiries into the matter:

Diedrich, who is Austrian, and his brother-in-law
Dorfman engage extensively in opium smuggling, and
are in the habit of employing women who have Russian
passports to bring the drug from Russian territory by
rail and boat to Shanghai.

This smuggling has been going on rather extensive-
ly for the past three years, and several members of the
pimp fraternity have amassed considerable money in the
trade. It is said that the majority of the Russian
and Chinese customs officials employed on the frontiers
are bribed by the smugglers, whom they allow to go and
come freely. After the smugglers pass Manzhouli
(满洲里) their baggage is not again examined till they
reach Shanghai. The Customs officer at this end of
the line is a Russian citizen, who was formerly a
French protected Turk. He does not seem to exert
himself very much searching for contraband.

On March 3 a police report was forwarded to
the effect that Diedrich was in the habit of making
excursions to outports, probably for the purpose of

回复您 5 月 17 日关于一名叫 Lazar

对此事调查的结果：

Diedrich 是奥地利人，他和他的妹夫（或姐夫）
Dorfman 大量从事鸦片走私活动，并惯于雇用持有俄罗斯
护照的女性，通过铁路和船只将毒品从俄罗斯领土运至上海。

这种走私活动在过去三年中相当猖獗，几名
皮条客团伙成员在此交易中积累了巨额财富。据说，受雇于边境的
大多数俄罗斯和中国海关官员都收受了走私者的贿赂，允许他们自由
往来。走私者经过满洲里后，他们的行李在抵达上海之前不再接受检查。该线路末端的
海关官员是一名俄罗斯公民，他以前是一名受法国保护的土耳其人。他似乎在搜查违禁品方面并不十分尽力。

3 月 3 日提交了一份警务报告，称 Diedrich 习惯前往
外埠进行短途旅行，可能是为了

visiting agents in these places. The primary business
of the gang, of which he is the leader, is smuggling.
However, he and his associates are people who would
stoop to anything for money. If during their trips
to Russia or elsewhere they came into possession of
information useful to the Central Powers, they would
not scruple to pass it on. They would also be likely to
undertake espionage, provided the risks were not great.
Diedrich is the proprietor of No's 11 and 12
North Szechuen Road, and it is likely that he keeps
smuggled opium on the premises from time to time,
though no proof of this has been found.
Owing to Diedrich's extensive organisation, it
is very difficult to bring smuggling home to
him, but it should be an easy matter for the Customs
Authorities to employ lady searchers, and put a stop
to the activities of his female accomplices, whose
persons and baggage should be examined en route as
well as at Lan Chu Li and Shanghai. It is useless
for the police to try to check opium smuggling
while the present slackness exists in the Customs
service.
Enquiries have failed to elicit any confirmation
of the assertion that Schmidt is in league with the
smugglers. In fact, during the last two years he
has reported to Headquarters the activities of these
people.

Yours sincerely,

od K McEwan
Captain-Superintendent of Police.

Shanghai Municipal Police.
970 24/5/17

CENTRAL POLICE Station.
23rd May, 1917.

REPORT ON Enemy Subjects and Opium Smuggling.

Made by D.S.Givens. Forwarded by Inspector

Sir,
Enquiries re attached go to show that Diedrich, who is Austrian, and his brother-in-law Dorfman engage extensively in opium smuggling, and are in the habit of employing women who have Russian passports to bring the drug from Russian territory by rail and boat to Shanghai.

This smuggling has been going on rather extensively for the past three years, and several members of the pimp fraternity have amassed considerable money in the trade. It is said that the majority of the Russian and Chinese customs officials employed on the frontiers are bribed by the smugglers, whom they allow to go and come freely. After the smugglers pass Man Chu Li (满洲里), their baggage is not again examined till they reach Shanghai. The Customs officer at this end of the line is a Russian citizen, who was formerly a French protected Turk. He does not seem to exert himself very much searching for contraband.

As mentioned in my report of 3rd March, Diedrich is in the habit of making excursions to outports, probably for the purpose of visiting agents in these places. The primary business of the gang of which he is the leader is smuggling. However he and his associates are people who would stop at anything for money. If during their trips to Russia or elsewhere they came into possession of information useful to the Central Powers, they would not scruple to pass it on. They would also be likely to undertake spying business, provided the risks were not great.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
970 1917年5月24日

中央巡捕房。
1917 年 5 月 23 日。

关于敌国侨民与鸦片走私的报告。

由 D.S.Givens 撰写。由督察转呈

先生，
关于附件的调查表明，奥地利人 Diedrich 和他的妹夫（或姐夫）Dorfman 大量从事鸦片走私活动，并惯于雇用持有俄罗斯护照的女性，通过铁路和船只将毒品从俄罗斯领土运至上海。

这种走私活动在过去三年中相当猖獗，几名皮条客团伙成员在此交易中积累了巨额财富。据说，受雇于边境的大多数俄罗斯和中国海关官员都收受了走私者的贿赂，允许他们自由往来。走私者经过满洲里后，他们的行李在抵达上海之前不再接受检查。该线路末端的海关官员是一名俄罗斯公民，他以前是一名受法国保护的土耳其人。他似乎在搜查违禁品方面并不十分尽力。

正如我在 3 月 3 日的报告中所述，Diedrich 习惯前往外埠进行短途旅行，可能是为了拜访这些地方的代理人。他是头目的该团伙的主要业务是走私。然而，他和他的同伙都是些为了钱不择手段的人。如果他们在前往俄罗斯或其他地方的途中获得了对同盟国（Central Powers）有用的信息，他们会毫不犹豫地将其传递出去。只要风险不大，他们也很可能从事间谍活动。

Shanghai Municipal Police.
No. 979
Date 3/3/17
CENTRAL POLICE Station.
3rd March, 1917.
REPORT ON Austrian Opium Smuggler.
Made by D.S.Givens. Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.
Sir,
It is reported that an Austrian named Diedrich, who resides at
No. 110 Chapco Road, and who lives by opium smuggling, makes
frequent excursions to outports and to places in the interior.
This man is about 40 years old, below medium height and of stout
build. He has a dark brown moustache and dark brown hair,
but is slightly bald. It is said that Diedrich is financed
(N.E.B.) by Ezra, who was formerly foreign secretary of the Bank of
Territorial Development.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D.S.Givens
Detective Sergeant.
Chief Detective Inspector.
（左侧批注：5/3 5/3 Ash 5/3）

此人约 40 岁，身高低于中等，体格粗壮。
